To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
citrinin and the mixture of citrinin with aflatoxin, increased the infectivity and multiplication of T. gondii in macrophages.
CTR-AFB 1 increased T. gondii infectivity and proliferation in murine macrophages in vitro.
the treatment of T. gondii tachozytes with CTR or CTR-AFB(1) increased the number of parasites in vitro, and that CTR-AFB (1) was more effective than CTR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of citrinin, alone and in association with AFB1 on the infectivity, proliferation, and viability of T. gondii.
the effect of citrinin, a mycotoxin produced by Penicillium citrinum, on Toxoplasmosis, and its interaction with aflatoxin, which is produced by Aspergillus parasiticus.
the effects of citrinin, alone or in association with afla toxin B1 on the infection of Toxopla gondii in macrophages.

the presence of CTR or CTR-AFB(1) in the medium of macrophage cultures, increased the infectivity of the parasite and its proliferation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTR and AFB1 are capable of inducing the proliferation of T gondii in macrophages, and that the effect is more evident in the case of CTR.
citrinin (10 mug/mL) and the mixture of citrinin (2 mug/mL) and aflatoxin B (0.04 mug/mL) increased the number of Toxopla gondii tachozytes recovered from the supernant of the infected macrophages.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CTR and CTR-AFB(1) are able to promote the proliferation of T. gondii, which may be related to a decrease in the production of NO and an increase of the production of TNF-alpha.
the association of citrinin with aflatoxin in macrophages increases the number of parasites recovered from both cells and the supernatant, and that the effect is more pronounced at 72 h of infection.
the presence of CTR and the mixture of toxins CTR-AFB 1 in the culture medium of infected macrophages increases the proliferation of Toxplasma gondii.
